Verdict. Faster on the supplied synthetic CLI workload. Five alternating unprofiled runs per side give a baseline median of 2.4731920036 seconds and fixed median of 0.1516271783 seconds. The reduction is 93.8691707685 percent. Baseline range is 2.3963094447 to 2.6022116682 seconds. Fixed range is 0.1335565727 to 0.1571981385 seconds. See benchmark/summary.json and the ten raw run records.
1. Limiter. Baseline profiling attributes 94.65 percent of sampled time to summarize. A separate diagnostic probe counts 80,000 parses, with 2164 ms in JSON.parse within 2212 ms summarize. Post-fix probe counts one parse. Post-fix profile attributes 26.8 percent to the CLI frame, 18.35 percent to summarize, 17.07 percent to program, 16.67 percent to garbage collection and 7.42 percent to file reading. The remaining path includes serial event JSON parsing and accumulation, allocation, runtime startup and file input. A single short post profile does not establish stable percentages for each component.
2. Tuning. Both sides run the documented command with Node v24.19.0, identical input files, inherited environment, fresh processes and no profiler. There are no documented batch, build or concurrency settings to tune. OS file pages may be warm after baseline profiling. The comparison does not claim cold-disk behavior or production tuning.
3. Limits. The removed repetition parses 2,744 rule bytes 80,000 times, about 219.5 million logical bytes. The 93.87 percent elapsed reduction is below the baseline summarize sample share of 94.65 percent, so the observed gain does not exceed that coarse removable-work bound. Sampling and instrumentation are approximate; neither diagnostic duration is substituted for the timed CLI metric.
4. Errors. All ten timed runs exit 0 with empty stderr. Every parsed output exactly equals expected.json. Every run accounts for 80,000 processed events, 74,171 accepted events and 5,829 rejected events, with all category totals checked.
5. Repeatability. Order is baseline then app repeated five times. Both measured ranges are disjoint by more than two seconds. The median gap exceeds observed run variation. No additional performance trial is needed to determine the target passed.
6. Relevance. The timed region begins before subprocess creation and ends after stdout/stderr capture and process completion. It includes startup, file input, both parses, accumulation and final JSON output. It is the public batch CLI, not the diagnostic helper probe.
7. Work. Full output validation follows each completed timed process. Profile and parse-probe runs are separate files and excluded from benchmark/summary.json. Fresh process state and per-call string-rule cache prevent reuse across the baseline and fixed runs.
Scope. Node on one four-core host, 2,780,924 event bytes, 2,744 rules bytes, one synthetic deterministic 80,000-event batch. No production, concurrent-service, cross-provider or broad-workload claim.
